prompt: Your team shipped a home-grown Web Application Firewall as HTTP middleware in front of the main API route group — it runs a blocklist of regex signatures for known SQL-injection and XSS payloads and returns a 403 when a request looks malicious. It compiles, and it blocks the obvious injection attempts on the happy-path demo. I want you to review this middleware the way you'd review a teammate's PR: walk me through exactly what it inspects, what it sends back when it blocks a request, and where it's mounted, then tell me what security holes and coverage gaps you'd flag before signing off on it as the team's real protection layer.
